title: Restricted-series finite presentations and bounded analytic models
statement: Let $R$ be a nonarchimedean normed commutative ring. The restricted-series ring $R\langle T_1,\ldots,T_n\rangle$ is the subring of formal power series whose coefficients tend to zero in the cofinite filter; constants are the constant series. For a ring map $\rho:R\to A$ and $\pi\in R$, say that $A$ is topologically finitely presented over $R$ if there are $n\geq0$ and a surjective ring map $f:R\langle T\rangle\to A$ with finitely generated kernel, $f|_R=\rho$, and the topology on $A$ is the quotient of the principal $\pi$-adic topology on the series ring (equivalently, the quotient map is a quotient map for the principal adic topologies). For a nonarchimedean normed field $F$ [def-weil-field] and a normed commutative ring $B$ with scalar map $F\to B$, an affinoid quotient presentation means that $B$ is complete and admits a surjective scalar-compatible ring map $F\langle T_1,\ldots,T_n\rangle\to B$ whose norm is the quotient Gauss norm: $\|b\|=\inf_{f(s)=b}\sup_\nu\|s_\nu\|$. The zero quotient is allowed. For maps $R\xrightarrow{\rho}A\xrightarrow j B$, the image of $A$ is bounded and topologically finitely generated over $R$ if $\|j(a)\|\le M$ for one real $M$ and all $a\in A$, and there are finitely many $x_i\in A$ such that every $j(a)$ is approximated arbitrarily closely in the norm of $B$ by polynomials in the $j(x_i)$ with coefficients in the image of $R$.
